title: Anyone else struggle with UI more than the actual game systems when using AI coding tools?
author: mtgkev
selftext:
I've been working on a dice-based roguelike in Godot for a few weeks, and I'm finding that UI is taking far more time than the actual game systems.

The gameplay side has been pretty straightforward and enjoyable to build. Units, attacks, shields, healing, enemies, relics, consumables, gear, abilities etc all have complicated systems that work perfectly. But every UI change seems to turn into a long back-and-forth with Claude, Cursor, or Codex. I've tried making mockups (including Claude Design) first and having AI implement them, but the final result in Godot never looks as clean as the mockup, and even small changes can take a lot of prompts to get right.

At this point I've probably spent 30 hours on the project, and it feels like half of that time has gone into UI alone. I can burn through Claude's usage limit in a single session just trying to fix layouts and styling.

Is this just a normal part of game development, or is there a better workflow for handling UI in Godot? I'm starting to feel like adding a new gameplay feature is easier than moving a few UI elements around.

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: Are you using godot mcp so the agent can see the output as it builds?

replies.author: mtgkev
replies.body: i havent hooked up the MCP specifically but claude has found a way to launch the game, do the necessary action, then take a screenshot and just from that. i'll look into the MCP since that seems like it may give claude more data to work with

replies.author: zorflax
replies.body: Do it. You'll wish you did it sooner once you install.

replies.author: Yenii_3025
replies.body: Someone else recently suggested having Claude take a screenshot before and after every implementation. Not sure it works though.

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
Godot MCP allows the ai to use the engine API directly and recieving the output like the engine creates it. Works so much better, way less bugs.
15 bugs for godot MCP pro is worth it

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
I mean, UI/UX is a hired position in companies. Some people only design UI/UX full time and that is it. 

so yeah, hobbyists and amateurs are going to struggle with UI and that is expected.

at least we got AI to help us out so there is that.

comments.author: Only-Discussion9421
comments.body: I’ve been focusing on the ui/ux towards the end of prototyping and development since things change so much during development. I build just a basic cookie cutter ui that only shows text placement, the containers are named though. This way when I am at a good place in the game, I consolidate different environments to apply different ui and if I mess up, I just restart the greybox it’s in. Once I feel good about it, I just apply it to the game assets since the naming convention all the same. This way it’s not impacting the core element of development since I’m easily distracted.

replies.author: mtgkev
replies.body: Yeah I made the mistake of doing UI up front first, but after trashing that I've been waiting to finalize it. I've put a lot into the backend and now i'm finalizing the UI and it's been frustrating, especially waiting for Claude's 5 hour lockouts. Good to know that this is probably the best way at least

comments.author: d-czar
comments.body:
I built a bunch of UI-specific tools into the Godot AI mcp. IMHO it’s pretty good at taking references and helping bring them to life. In this post I showed a completely procedural set of UI elements I built with it (no generative art, no sprites).  It links to the repo for the UI demo if you want to check it out. 

https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/s/GTrQMr3Fsu

comments.author: PleasantCitron1685
comments.body:
The UI needs to connect properly to your game's backend, so if your backend is not well-designed, you're going to have lots and lots of duplicated and hard to maintain code.

If it is spending all that time just to connect the UI elements correctly, it's not going to be able to help much with design.

You can try making it design the UI in a fresh project and having it connect to the main use case afterwards.

comments.author: Helpful-Account3311
comments.body: I’ve been using Claude with Unity lately.  In Unity at least I’ve had a lot of luck by putting a line in my Claude.md saying all UI changes should be done via one off editor scripts.

replies.author: mtgkev
replies.body: thanks ill give that a try in godot!

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: I actually like UI. To build something easy and interesting and intuitive to use is a bit of a fun exercise for me.

comments.author: Kingnorik
comments.body: You have to let other people try the game and listen to their complaints. Like your friends and family. Tell them to be brutal and tear it down with what works and what they don't like. Take that info and try to Gen some mockups

comments.author: BertJohn
comments.body:
UI in all engines is bad for AI except for the UI Toolkit in unity. 

  
UI Toolkit has a very close resemblance to existing trained data so it can produce far easier. Godot's UI, UE, And even unity's UGUI will cook your tokens non-stop. It's simply due to the lack of trained data that its struggling to create the intended final product.

comments.author: tschilpi
comments.body: Holy I remember pre newest models how insanely hard it was to code UIs as a solodev. To make them responsive, etc. Compared to that it's a piece of cake with modern AI lol

comments.author: Southern_Charge5794
comments.body: I have had the same issue. My understanding is that all those AI model does not have so much training data related to Godot UI. It always were different in editor and in real scene and when you see the code you wanna cry as it always over-complicate the solution, trying to do things dynamically and etc. Approach that did help me is to refactor one scene into composition that I like and after that things became better and it finally started to make things right after I gave him good references.
